card.name: Pentozali
card.era: 18th c. (music credited to Cretan violinist Stefanos Triantafillakis, c. 1770-1771)
card.tagline: Fast Cretan war dance of high leaps and improvisation.
card.profile: The trademark folk dance of Crete; a vigorous war dance with high jumping movements and improvisation. Name from pente ('five') + zalos ('step/jump') - 'five-steps,' the dance having ten steps; also punned with zali ('dizziness'). Dancers form an incomplete counterclockwise circle, arms on shoulders; the lead dancer improvises acrobatic leaps while the second holds his hand as a stable base. Starts moderate and accelerates. Instrumental music: the melody on Cretan lyra (or violin) with percussive laouto accompaniment; the lyra player directs the dance's flow (English Wikipedia; Music of Crete).
card.insight: Tradition links pentozali to Cretan uprisings against the Ottomans - said to symbolize the 'fifth attempt' to liberate Crete; the music is credited to Stefanos Triantafillakis around 1770-1771 (English Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: Crete's dizzying warrior dance. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Crete, Greece.
